mcqs.question: Consider the domain D = ℝ (all real numbers). Which of the following correctly compares the truth values of the two universal statements (i) ∀x ∈ D, x > 0 and (ii) ∀x ∈ D, x ≥ 0 ?

options.C: Statement (i) is true and statement (ii) is false.
options.D: Statement (i) is false and statement (ii) is true.

mcqs.explanation: Over the set of all real numbers there exist numbers that are zero or negative. Hence the statement "for every real x, x > 0" is false, and the statement "for every real x, x ≥ 0" is also false because negative numbers violate it. Therefore both universal statements are false.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly uses the existential quantifier to assert that there exists an integer n such that n² = 25?
mcqs.explanation: The existential quantifier (∃) states that at least one element of the domain satisfies the given property. Option B correctly says that there exists an integer whose square equals 25 (namely n = 5 or n = -5). The other options either use the universal quantifier or assert the opposite property.

mcqs.question: Translate the English statement into a quantified mathematical statement: "Every natural number is greater than or equal to zero."
mcqs.explanation: The phrase "Every natural number" calls for the universal quantifier (∀). The condition "is greater than or equal to zero" is expressed as n ≥ 0. Hence the correct translation is ∀n ∈ ℕ, n ≥ 0.

mcqs.question: What is the correct negation of the universal statement ∀x ∈ ℝ, x² ≥ 0 ?
mcqs.explanation: The negation of a universal statement ∀x P(x) is the existential statement ∃x ¬P(x). Here P(x) is "x² ≥ 0", so ¬P(x) is "x² < 0". Therefore the negation is ∃x ∈ ℝ, x² < 0. Options A, C, and D do not represent the correct logical negation.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines the universal quantifier and distinguishes it from the existential quantifier?

options.A: The universal quantifier (∀) states that a property holds for at least one element, whereas the existential quantifier (∃) states it holds for all elements.
options.B: The universal quantifier (∀) states that a property holds for all elements of the domain, while the existential quantifier (∃) states that there exists at least one element for which the property holds.
options.C: Both quantifiers mean the same; they are interchangeable.
options.D: The universal quantifier (∀) is used only for finite domains, while the existential quantifier (∃) is used only for infinite domains.

mcqs.answer: The universal quantifier (∀) states that a property holds for all elements of the domain, while the existential quantifier (∃) states that there exists at least one element for which the property holds.
mcqs.explanation: Option B correctly captures the meaning of the two quantifiers: ∀ asserts that the predicate is true for every element, whereas ∃ asserts the existence of at least one element making the predicate true. The other options contain incorrect definitions or irrelevant distinctions.

mcqs.question: In a class of 30 students, the statement "There is a student who scored above 90 marks" is an example of which quantifier?
mcqs.explanation: The phrase "There is a student" asserts the existence of at least one student with the described property, which is precisely the role of the existential quantifier (∃). It does not claim that all students have the property, so it is not universal.

mcqs.question: Select the option that correctly translates the quantified statement: ∃x ∈ ℤ such that x is odd.

options.A: There exists an integer x that is odd.
options.D: For every integer x, x is odd.

mcqs.answer: There exists an integer x that is odd.
mcqs.explanation: The symbol ∃ denotes existence. Hence ∃x ∈ ℤ, x is odd means "There exists an integer x that is odd." Options B, C, and D misinterpret the quantifier.

mcqs.question: A teacher claims: "It is not true that every student in the class has submitted the assignment." Which of the following is the correct logical negation of the teacher's claim?

options.A: All students have submitted the assignment.
options.B: No student has submitted the assignment.
options.C: At least one student has not submitted the assignment.
options.D: Exactly one student has submitted the assignment.

mcqs.answer: At least one student has not submitted the assignment.
mcqs.explanation: The teacher's statement is the negation of the universal claim ∀x (Student x has submitted). Negating a universal yields an existential statement: ∃x (Student x has not submitted). This is expressed as "At least one student has not submitted the assignment." Options A and B are opposite extremes, and D is unrelated.
